The proposed answer, $\frac{8\pi}{3}+2\sqrt{3}\approx 11.841682$, is correct.

**Speed:** $f'(\theta)=ie^{i\theta}(1+e^{i\theta})^2$, so $|f'(\theta)|=|1+e^{i\theta}|^2=2+2\cos\theta=4\cos^2(\theta/2)$. The full curve has length $\int_0^{2\pi}4\cos^2(\theta/2)\,d\theta=4\pi$.

**Self-intersections:** Write $z=e^{i\theta}$ and $f=z+z^2+z^3/3$. For $f(z_1)=f(z_2)$ with $z_1\neq z_2$ on the unit circle, set $s=z_1+z_2$ and $p=z_1z_2$. This gives $p=s^2+3s+3$. Writing $z_1=e^{ia}$, $z_2=e^{ib}$, with $w=e^{i(a+b)/2}$ and $c=2\cos\frac{a-b}{2}$, the condition becomes $(1-c^2)w-3\bar w=3c$. The imaginary part forces $w=\pm1$ or $c=\pm2$. The case $c=\pm2$ means $z_1=z_2$, so it is excluded. The remaining cases all give the single pair $\{e^{2\pi i/3},e^{4\pi i/3}\}$, so $f(2\pi/3)=f(4\pi/3)=-\tfrac23$ is the only self-intersection.

**Nesting:** The winding number of the curve about $w$ equals the number of zeros of $z^3/3+z^2+z-w$ inside $|z|<1$. At $w=0$ this is 1, so the outer region has winding number 1. At $w=-\tfrac12$ the zeros of $(z+1)^3+\tfrac12$ include two with $|z|\approx0.914<1$, so the winding number is 2. Both loops are counterclockwise and the inner loop lies inside the outer one. Its interior is therefore part of $R$, not a hole, and the perimeter is the outer loop alone.

**Outer loop length:** It consists of $\theta\in[0,2\pi/3]$ and $\theta\in[4\pi/3,2\pi]$. Each piece contributes $\int 2(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta$:
- $\int_0^{2\pi/3}2(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}+\sqrt3$
- $\int_{4\pi/3}^{2\pi}2(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta=\frac{4\pi}{3}+\sqrt3$

The total is $\frac{8\pi}{3}+2\sqrt3$. The inner loop has length $\frac{4\pi}{3}-2\sqrt3$, and the two loops sum to $4\pi$, which checks out.

The numerical value $\frac{8\pi}{3}+2\sqrt3 = 11.841682024710536$ matches the stated final answer.
